items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — Depressants by Defect Designer is an interesting blend of Avant Garde with technical death metal from the Russian trio. A band with the attitude of "let's see what happens if we mix this together," it overall does showcase some interesting results, with the band genre hopping all over the place so much that even the James Bond theme turns up randomly. While the production is a bit on the weak side, there's enough there to entertain, but it would be good to see them put their talents into something more focused. I'd give this a mid to high 6 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is Expectation Request Referral Denied.
items._genre: avant-garde metal / technical death metal / progressive metal
items._cn_summary: 俄罗斯三人乐队Defect Designer在这张专辑中将先锋实验精神注入技术死亡金属，呈现出一种近乎随性的拼贴态度。乐队在类型间频繁跳跃，甚至将007詹姆斯·邦德主题曲毫无预兆地植入金属结构中，展现出强烈的解构与重组意愿。专辑尝试打破技术死亡的固有框架，融合前卫与极端金属的表现手法，创造出难以预测的听觉路径。然而制作略显粗糙，诸多想法虽有趣却缺乏聚焦，未能将零散的灵感整合为更完整的艺术表达。整体而言，这是一张展示了实验野心但尚需精炼的作品，对于热衷于跨类型探索的听众而言值得一听。

items.body: Enter Mephistopheles Overcome by innocence and purity On a hell-bent path led to corrupt To destroy us all and rise above Goth music has always been hospitable to transformation: flesh into apparition, desire into doctrine, the nightclub into a temporary chapel. Pittsburgh industrial project ShadowMouth and Cleveland vocal trio The Elder Goths take that appetite for metamorphosis literally on The Promise of Alchemy/The Death of Chemistry, a paired single released August 12th and the final preview of ShadowMouth’s forthcoming debut album, Modern Alchemy. ShadowMouth is the project of multi-instrumentalist and songwriter Rick Polo, of Baroque Monody and Heck Vektor, with producer and drummer Brooks Farris of Electric Fox Studios. After the 2024 EP Purification By Fire and singles including Your Words, Not Mine and DOOM SCROLLERS vs HOLY ROLLERS, Polo reached outside his immediate circle for these two pieces, contacting The Elder Goths: Cassandra Bishop, Laura O’Janpa, and Gina Schultz, without having met them. “These songs were the result of me taking a shot in the dark and reaching out The Elder Goths group, who I had never met before, and asked if they would provide some of the striking beautifully haunting harmonies that are immediately apparent when first hearing their work,” says Polo. “But it turned out to be so much more than I could have imagined. The end result was an intense and and really heartfelt delivery which absolutely blew me away. This collaboration felt too important not to highlight. So we decided to release this a single ahead of the record.” That gamble pays off immediately on The Promise of Alchemy. Aphex Twin-like electronics move beneath spare guitar passages while Bishop’s lyrics describe awakening, perception, and the search for one’s place within a larger atmosphere. The Elder Goths bring an elegant, spectral grandeur that recalls Strange Boutique, Faith and the Muse, and the ceremonial scale of Dead Can Dance. Their layered voices give Polo’s machinery a sense of upward motion, turning alchemy into a metaphor for people entering the same space and becoming altered by the encounter. The Death of Chemistry, with lyrics by Schultz, pushes the collaboration toward darker territory. Its language circles blindness, consumption, manipulation, predation, and the dangerous seductions of appearances. Mephistopheles enters as an emblem of corruption, while bodily warnings – alarm, dread, instinctive recoil – suggest a consciousness struggling to recognize danger before persuasion overrides perception. The final image of being taken in by a “suntan and a grin” gives the song a wickedly contemporary sting: evil may arrive beautifully groomed, socially fluent, and camera-ready. Together, the songs form a compact study in attraction and corruption. One considers transformation as revelation; the other examines how easily perception can be bent by charisma, appetite, and spectacle. This tension gives the collaboration a compelling force, especially because the music itself began with an act of trust between strangers. Listen below and purchase the double single here. The Promise of Alchemy/The Death of Chemistry by ShadowMouth & The Elder Goths Formed in 2024 after its members crossed paths through Cleveland’s underground scene, The Elder Goths will perform at Pagan Pride Fest in Cleveland on August 15th. Their appearance on Modern Alchemy gives ShadowMouth’s coming album an intriguing final preview: four musicians meeting across projects and cities, testing what might happen when unfamiliar elements are placed in the same vesse Follow ShadowMouth: Instagram Facebook Bandcamp Follow The Elder Goths: Instagram Bandcamp The post ShadowMouth and The Elder Goths Collaborate on Twin Tracks “The Promise of Alchemy and The Death of Chemistry” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 匹兹堡工业计划ShadowMouth与克利夫兰人声三重唱The Elder Goths合作推出双单曲《炼金术之诺/化学之死》，作为首张专辑《现代炼金术》的终曲预览。制作人Rick Polo在Aphex Twin式电子纹理与稀疏吉他段落之上，叠加The Elder Goths分层和声，呈现出类似Strange Boutique、Faith and the Muse及Dead Can Dance的庄严幽灵气质。《炼金术之诺》以觉醒与感知为主题，将人声与机械音色交织，暗示相遇带来的蜕变；《化学之死》则以梅菲斯托为象征，剖析盲目、操控与伪装，歌词揭示邪恶可能以光鲜外表登场。两曲构成关于吸引与腐化的紧凑对照，融合工业电子骨架与哥特美学的仪式感，探索跨地域合作中声音与意义的化学反应。

items._cn_summary: 这是芝加哥独立厂牌Kino Disk发行的第二张合作专辑，由来自印第安纳波利斯的制作人Eustress（Heath Gillespie）操刀。整张专辑延续了他对dub techno类型的深度探索，六首曲目在熟悉的手法上做出了有意识的扭曲与变形处理。制作人大量运用飘渺、模糊的混响效果处理dub和弦，营造出广阔而充满风感的音景空间，将dub techno原本冷峻、机械的骨架柔化为更具氛围感的声场。厂牌长期聚焦于前卫电子与抽象声音艺术的发行脉络，与底特律-芝加哥地下电子传统形成对话。专辑呈现出对根源的尊重与个人化诠释之间的平衡，在氛围铺陈与节奏结构之间保持了张力。

items._cn_summary: Chris Connelly 是 Ministry 与 Finitribe 的重要成员，此作以个人项目之名汇聚十二首作品，构建出一套不安而陌生的聆听体验。整张专辑以拼贴手法为核心：具体音乐式的剪接碎片、被切裂的旋律、压抑的低噪，以及看似随机的现场录音交织在一起。Connelly 的声线让人联想到 Bowie 演绎经典时期作品的方式，低沉而疏离。专辑横跨新民谣的奇想、军事音乐的庄严、苏格兰声音诗的冷峻，以及工业声响的粗糙边缘。Connelly 与 Burroughs、C93 之间存在明显的美学血缘——文学性的拼贴、反叛的姿态、对权威叙事的拆解。作品既是对工业音乐传统的延续，也是一次向更广阔实验领域延伸的尝试，呈现出碎片化叙事与声响探索的双重张力。

items._cn_summary: 这是挪威与英伦演奏家的首张合作专辑，以踏板吉他为核心，辅以管风琴、Moog合成器与鼓机，呈现朦胧、水平铺展的二重奏质地。评论将作品置于Suzanne Alcorn与Daniel Lanois之间的光谱中，暗示其既承袭踏板吉他滑音编织的声景传统，又带有实验氛围的质地。踏板吉他作为氛围乐器的潜力被再次确认，尤其在Lanois为Eno《Apollo》专辑引入该音色后，这一路径有了明确的参照。段落如同一段缓慢飘移的对话，乐器间的呼吸与留白构成主体，没有密集的节奏推进，而是以音色渐变与和声温度变化为骨干。整张专辑以简约编制营造出沉浸式的听觉空间，适合作为背景聆听，却也保留了足够的细节供主动聆听者探寻。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是芬兰电子音乐人 Mika Vainio（Pan Sonic 成员之一）于2017年逝世后遗作的正式发行，被视为其个人创作的巅峰之作。整张作品如同一组声波明信片，勾勒出由离散声岛组成的遥远群岛意象，音乐在极简的质感中呈现出高度个人化的情绪纹理。压轴曲 'Loputon' 被认为是其遗产中最为珍贵的篇章之一，既是这位艺术家漫长创作生涯的终章，也是对其深远影响的致敬。专辑延续了 Vainio 一贯的丰富表现力极简主义路线，将冷峻的电子声响与内省的氛围营造结合，在有限的音色中构建出绵延的心理空间。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这是Bongo Joe厂牌发行的圣多美和普林西比70-80年代音乐合集第二卷，记录了非洲葡语国家小岛在所谓黄金时代的Puxa舞曲风貌。乐评指出该音乐融合merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等多种元素，与葡萄牙殖民历史及跨大西洋地理位置有关，但其声音仍独具岛屿特色。15首作品中多把吉他交织缠绕，主唱与和声形成旋律框架，乐手如Pedro Lima的乐队展示强烈的失真吉他与鼓的对抗，Africa Negra的作品则展现放克律动。文章强调Puxa具有召魂驱魔的仪式功能，与当地文化深度绑定。该合集由独立小厂牌发行，聚焦罕见的非洲小岛音乐档案，具有独特的文化保存价值。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦贝宁传奇乐团Orchestre Poly-Rythmo与歌手Antoine Dougbé在1977至1982年间的合作作品。Dougbé被称为"魔鬼首相"，同时是伏都教实践者，他以拍击大腿创造的Cavacha节奏著称，该节奏由鼓手Belobi Meridjo从火车节奏中提炼，后广泛传播于1970年代中期的刚果流行乐中。专辑中音乐融合伏都教仪式的根源律动、古巴son影响的明亮和声与旋律，以及席卷撒哈拉以南非洲的刚果伦巴元素。录制受时代限制，吉他带有塑料质感光泽，合成器开始出现，为整体增添八十年代音色色彩。曲目如《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》以合成器铺垫开场，闪亮吉他与高频踩镲主导节奏；《We Tayi Sin Assi Tche》则呈现更明显的古巴风格，以持续牛铃与鼻音唱腔呼应结构。作为Analog Africa厂牌推出的第四十四号发行，这是该厂牌继三张精选集与一张首张专辑再版之后，对Poly-Rythmo音乐版图的又一次系统性挖掘。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 乐队的这张专辑以手工自制的非常规乐器为核心特色，乐评详细列举了他们用废旧材料制作的多种独创乐器，并在录音中展现出令人印象准确的音准与丰富的音质。专辑融合了多种世界音乐风格：克莱兹默曲调由笑声般的人声与巴松管搭配，昆比亚段落配以西班牙语合唱与拉丁打击乐，非洲节奏段落散布木鱼、沙锤与铃铛，桑巴段落的笛声与中东曲调则展现出跨文化的即兴演奏能力。即兴段落展现了乐手扎实的演奏功底。整张专辑传达的核心信息是：音乐人总能找到方式用任何材料创造音乐，即使面对现代乐器泛滥的时代，手工与创意仍能让音乐焕发独特生命力。这是一张充满趣味与实验精神的世界音乐跨界作品。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio
items.label: Taragot
items._genre: experimental jazz / folk fusion / improvisation / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由挪威的Camilla Hole Trio演奏，主奏乐器为高音萨克斯，搭配贝斯、鼓和模块合成器、颤音琴等元素。乐评重点描述了开篇曲目《Springleik》的结构与编排——作品源自挪威西部的传统弹簧舞曲旋律，先由萨克斯陈述主调，贝斯与鼓提供节奏支撑，随后加入合成器与颤音琴丰富音色层次。乐评特别指出这支三人组的角色分配并不固定，贝斯手Kalman接手旋律与萨克斯齐奏，鼓手Nesheim则进一步拓展节奏维度，使整首作品逐渐走向即兴展开，萨克斯在尾声再次回到旋律。相较于前作《Eventyrferd》中科幻合成器与传统素材的大胆嫁接，《Langs》回归更具大地感的表达，但仍延续了对挪威本土民间音乐之外更广阔语汇的探索。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由电子声学作曲家弗洛里安·维滕堡与柏林出生的作曲家卡斯滕·戴尔合作呈现，收录于Wandelweiser厂牌旗下，以简约的六面板包装发行CD。整张专辑仅由三个短暂片段构成，核心是戴尔创作的一首温暖且动人的独奏钢琴作品，标题即为"Blessings"，乐评将其比作阳光在平静湖面上的反射。维滕堡的电子声学构思与戴尔的学院派钢琴语汇形成微妙对话，整体呈现出安静、内省的聆听体验，适合在静谧环境中细细品味。专辑时长极短，倾向于以极简的篇幅传递声音的质感与氛围，属于当代古典与电子声学交汇地带的探索性作品。

items.body: Never mess with Murdoch’s society Crashing and burning oh what a pity Tracky Nike fourth reich vitriol spray Commonplace everyday wreck of the UK Modern life has become one long argument with a screen, a boss, a stranger, a lover, or the idiot currently screaming beneath a flag in a supermarket car park. Shaven Primates have mined the exhaustion and alchemized it into a new EP, Kill The Algorithm. The Oxford quartet turns private dependency, political resentment, male grievance, and algorithmic manipulation into four rough-and-tumble songs powered by post-punk tension, industrial abrasion, art-rock unease, and guitars that sound ready to put somebody through a wall. Saviour starts from the most private wound. Its language treats affection as narcotic relief, the beloved transformed into medicine for absences that began much earlier, somewhere around the missing mother, missing father, and the suspicion that another person might finally close the hole. The 1990s references make sense: Placebo’s bruised glamour, Nine Inch Nails’ compulsive machinery, A Perfect Circle’s heavy-lidded grandeur. The emotional centre remains ugly enough to feel dangerous. Love becomes dosage, fantasy becomes diagnosis, and the repeated appeal to a saviour keeps curdling into evidence that salvation has been outsourced to somebody equally mortal. Pioneer Way drags that anxiety into public, where the nervous breakdown has flags tied to the lamp posts. The track takes aim at a Britain of workplace exhaustion, tabloid conditioning, immigrant scapegoating, screen addiction, and everyday fury looking for a body to blame. There is something grimly comic about a man screaming at an indicator while the country around him rehearses imperial fantasies beside a roundabout. The Sex Pistols influence is less about imitation than permission: permission to sneer at the pageantry, to notice how easily personal failure gets repackaged as national grievance, and to turn the resulting disgust into a hook sharp enough to draw blood. Then Feed goes after the salesmen. These are the grievance merchants who discover lonely young men, tell them tenderness is weakness, sell coercion as confidence, and monetize every insecurity they helped aggravate. The band brings in the clenched attack of Rage Against the Machine and Metallica, but the song’s ugliest idea is economic. Misery has become a business model. The customer is kept hungry because a satisfied customer might stop clicking. That thought detonates fully in Kill The Algorithm, where social media becomes less a tool than a delivery system for appetite, paranoia, tribal identity, and manufactured certainty. Radiohead, Black Sabbath and Iron Maiden hover in the architecture, while the repeated command at the song’s centre turns disgust into something nearly ecstatic. The target is the machine that keeps learning which wound to prod next. Listen to Kill The Algorithm below: Shaven Primates have made four songs about dependence: on lovers, on screens, on enemies, on gurus, on systems that promise relief while feeding the sickness. The riffs grind, the drums hit with factory-floor force, and the vocals move from wounded croon to open-throated accusation. The EP is held together by the recognition that private desperation and public brutality are often roommates, splitting the rent while each insists the other started the fire. Follow Shaven Primates: Instagram YouTube TikTok Facebook The post “You Prey on Those You Feed” — Oxford Quartet Shaven Primates Share “Kill The Algorithm” EP appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 牛津四人乐队Shaven Primates在这张EP中将私人情感依赖、政治怨气、男性怨懑与算法操控熔铸为四首粗粝之作。首曲以亲密创伤开场，将爱欲比作缓解缺失的药方，反复呼唤救赎却发现救赎同样来自凡人。第二首将焦虑推向公共空间，瞄准疲惫职场、小报洗脑与替罪叙事，Sex Pistols式的嘲讽成为刺入现实的钩子。第三首剖析怨气商人如何将孤独青年的不安全感变现，揭示苦难已成为商业模式。终曲则将社交媒体定位为欲望、偏执与部落身份的输送系统，重复的指令将厌恶推向近乎狂喜的状态。整体制作融合后朋克张力、工业粗粝、艺术摇滚不安与随时可能将人推入墙内的吉他音色，引用谱系涵盖Placebo、Nine Inch Nails、Rage Against the Machine直至Radiohead与Iron Maiden。

items.body:
Trane’s first album as bandleader surfaces on Craft Recordings’ guided reissue tour of classic jazz totems, spotlighting a vital period of modal jazz development from his years with the Prestige label, circa playing with Thelonious Monk and Miles Davis.

Recorded in May, 1957 and published in September that year, ’Coltrane’ marks the point when the great saxophonist began to transcend the acclaim of his peers for much wider recognition, with record sales numbers to follow suit. At the head of band including Red Garland on keys, Paul Chambers’ bass, Albert Heath on sticks, and Sahib Shihab’s baritone sax, Coltrane’s sound matures with a unique balance of smoky quintessence and modal experimentalism that would greatly inform jazz music in moving forward, outward.

That's all ideally illustrated on the daring modal suss of opener ‘Bakai’ with its switches between dervishing brass and angular rhythm to cooler stroll, and the contrast with its proceeding ‘Violets for your Furs’, and again in the closing couplet of ‘While My Lady Sleeps’ with its almost frenzied darts between the romantic and curiously exotic, and extended jazz-blues trip ‘Chronic Blues’.
items._genre: modal jazz / hard bop / early free jazz
items._cn_summary: 这是约翰·柯川作为乐队领队的首张专辑，1957年录制于Prestige厂牌时期，标志着他从同伴赞誉走向更广泛认可的转折点。乐队编制包括钢琴Red Garland、贝斯Paul Chambers、鼓手Albert Heath及巴洛克萨克斯Sahib Shihab。专辑展现了柯川在硬波普框架内对调式爵士的探索，音色在烟雾般凝练的抒情性与螺旋上升的实验性之间取得平衡。开场曲Bakai在炽烈铜管与锐利节奏间快速切换，Violets for your Furs形成情绪对比；尾曲While My Lady Sleeps在浪漫与异域情调间急促穿行，Chronic Blues则展开一段延伸的爵士蓝调即兴。整张作品预示了柯川此后将开创的自由爵士方向，是其艺术轨迹中的关键早期节点。

items.body:
All upward lift and kosmiche synth iridescence from Seoul’s blissed family band, back on the Far East’s leading krautrock revival label, Guruguru Brain...

“The blissed family band is back! TENGGER have always moved together, through time, space & genre. 'SKY' arrives as a new chapter: a little more still, a little more inward, while keeping all the warmth that's always been at the heart of what they do.

Embodying the band name meaning "endless sky" in Mongolian and "vast sea" in Hungarian, their 8th album 'SKY' centres on the feelings of boundless, infinite expansion. Conceived as one continuous environment rather than a collection of tracks, the album unfolds slowly through luminous synths, patient drones and Itta's breath-like vocals.

Like a soft big sky you can actually float on: 'SKY' is vast, warm, and wide open.

"Rather than a specific emotion, we hope the record opens a certain awareness — that the sky is not just something to be seen. Through it, we sense a connection to something much larger — a feeling of being linked to the wider universe. This sense of connection runs through the entire record.””
items._genre: kosmische / ambient / krautrock revival / drone / synth-based
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自首尔家族乐队TENGGER，由Guruguru Brain厂牌发行。乐评将其定位为krautrock复兴系列中的升腾型作品，强调合成器的光泽感和持续展开的氛围结构。整张专辑被构想为一个连贯的整体而非独立曲目的集合，通过发光的合成音色、耐心的低频持续音和Itta如呼吸般的声线缓慢铺陈。专辑名'SKY'对应乐队名在蒙古语中'无尽天空'、匈牙利语中'浩瀚海洋'的含义，探讨的是无边无际的无限扩展感。乐队自身陈述表明，他们希望这张作品开启某种意识——天空不只是被观看的对象，透过它感知与更宏大事物的联结，这种贯穿全作的连接感构成了专辑的核心概念。

items.body:
Custom-built for sunny days, Sofie Birch’s solo Stroom debut melds bossa and psych pops with delicate touches of 4th world ambient jazz and chamber music in a chiffon-layered, naïf dream sequence landing somewhere on the line between Sam Prekop's self-titled alltimer, Antena's Camino Del Sol x Stereolab on the downbeat...

"This album is created over the past years with my brother Alfred. This period has been spiritually transformative for me. it reflects the playfulness and authenticity that comes out of releasing deep traumas and healing wounds. this music comes from a deep place of joy and connection with my brother and with the essense of being a child. being filter free and in contact with the most uncomplicated and loving parts of ourselves, still emphasizing magic and mystery, like childhood does without asking for permission or confirmation.

It took me a while to actually see the music as an interconnected piece. i have been taking in and out material, re mixing, removing, rearranging, re producing and regretting all along the way. but suddenly when we mastered this selection on a cassette tape recorder, the meaning started to reveal itself and drawing threads back in time.

Bivabippalukka is playfulness, intuition, transition and myths. the page of cups. the ideas rising, the energy flowing, flowers, stars and jumping creatures on the verge of dimensions. fortune telling, magic cards, secret caves and things that disappear right in front of you. many talented guests playing with me and my visions on the album.

Bossa nova is the most comforting genre for me. and we need comfort in these times. we need comfort to heal and feel joy to be able to keep dreaming and manifesting - and transmuting the world.

I am not gonna play this music live in the form it appears. i will still continue playing spiritual ambient music. this work is something else. it is pocket of joy, a cup with a fish. it is a step on the journey, like everything else."
items._cn_summary: Sofie Birch 的首张个人专辑将巴萨诺瓦与迷幻流行编织在一起，融入第四世界氛围爵士和室内乐元素，营造出轻盈透明的梦境质感。唱片由她与兄弟 Alfred 历时多年协作完成，从最初零散素材到卡带母带处理后才显现整体意义，强调释放创伤、重拾童真与直觉游戏的过程。她将巴萨诺瓦视为当今时代最需要的慰藉类型，以此承载疗愈与快乐。专辑伴随多位客座乐手参与，以塔罗牌"杯之侍者"为核心意象，构建关于直觉、过渡与神话的叙事。厂牌 Stroom 属小众独立发行，整体定位介于 Sam Prekop 风格的简约与 Stereolab 的节拍实验之间，是一张带有自我疗愈诉求的跨界作品。

items._cn_summary: 慕尼黑现代艺术博物馆Brandhorst围绕John Cage、Merce Cunningham、Jasper Johns、Robert Rauschenberg与Cy Twombly等艺术家的作品策划了系列声音与实验音乐项目。本专辑汇集了多位艺术家对这一展览的回应，涵盖声音诗、前卫环境流行、technoid脉冲律动以及水下氛围等多种风格路径。作品试图将视觉艺术的概念与声音实验相连接，呈现出从诗歌朗诵到电子脉冲的宽广光谱，体现了策展型合辑的实验性与多元性。由于正文内容较短且偏向展览介绍性质，专辑的细节安排与各曲目的创作意图未能完全展开。

items.body: REWORK have been around long enough to know that club music’s supposedly clean breaks with the past are usually rather messier affairs. Michael Kübler and Daniel Varga formed the Stuttgart electronic project in 2000 with French vocalist Laetitia Rometsch, releasing their first EP, Anyway I Know You, through Frankfurt’s Playhouse Records. Their 2003 debut album, Fall Right Now, brought together early cuts, including “You’re So Just Just,” and established the combination they would come to describe as “new wave house”: spare machines, clipped funk, European pop instincts, and vocals that regard seduction as a form of mild antagonism. Later records for Playhouse, Visionquest, Get Physical, and their own Exlove imprint continued to complicate the boundaries between house, techno, electro, and pop at a time when those distinctions still carried considerable tribal weight. Released through Exlove Records on July 17th, the three-track Disco Love Remixes EP returns to the title track of REWORK’s March 2025 release. The original followed 2024’s Never Again and a Get Physical release that paired REWORK’s updated version of “You’re So Just Just” with separate remixes by Cinthie and Seth Troxler with Ryan Crosson. The new collection brings together interpretations by Neu-Romancer and Jennifer Touch alongside REWORK’s own “Disco Love2,” a special edit that reaches back toward the economical architecture of their Playhouse years. Sira Kübler’s vocal gives “Disco Love” its human temperature, sitting against bass and percussion disciplined enough to make each small adjustment feel consequential. The Playhouse influence is explicit in “Disco Love2,” although the track avoids becoming an exercise in period reconstruction. Its disco vocabulary has been pared down until glamour becomes something harder, stranger and slightly severe. Neu-Romancer is the solo project of Laura Bailey, an Australian musician, producer and DJ originally from Fremantle and now based in Berlin. Her 2023 debut EP, Neue Romantika, appeared on Zanias’ Fleisch Records, drawing on Italo disco, darkwave, EBM, and New Romantic references across four original tracks and a Zanias remix. The record included “Remnants,” a collaboration with Kris Baha, while Bailey’s broader history includes playing bass with goth outfit VV & The Void and punk band CIERN, as well as performing in Zanias’ live group. Her connection with REWORK predates the present remix: the artists released the two-track Call You Up EP together in June 2025. For “Disco Love,” Neu-Romancer takes the material into a more insistent space. Her remix thickens the rhythmic motion and introduces a bouncing, almost predatory momentum, making the track feel as if it were designed for the point in a club night when conversation has ceased to be useful. Details accumulate without clutter, and the arrangement maintains a peculiar forward pressure even as its gestures become more expansive. Neu-Romancer Jennifer Touch is a Berlin-based producer, singer, live musician and DJ whose work draws in part on her upbringing in eastern Germany. After issuing her first solo record in 2014, she developed a body of work that moves freely between post-punk, industrial electronics, wave music and club production. Her albums Behind the Wall and Midnight Proposals appeared through FatCat Records in 2020 and 2023, respectively, followed by Aging at Airports through Fabrika Records in September 2025. She has also released music through Riotvan, Eskimo Recordings, and Live at Robert Johnson, and has collaborated with Curses and Paranoid London. Touch approaches “Disco Love” from another angle, bringing greater emotional abrasion to its polished frame. Her version pairs cold-wave textures with a forceful club structure, allowing tension to build around Sira Kübler’s vocals and the regimented percussion. The bass bears down with greater weight while the upper register remains brittle and exposed. It is an effective reminder of how closely post-punk’s severity and dance music’s physicality have always sat beside one another. Jennifer Touch That relationship between post-punk and dance music also explains the logic behind Exlove Records, REWORK’s own imprint. Its catalog moves between synthpop, house, techno, electro, post-punk and synthwave without treating genre boundaries as border control, with releases from REWORK alongside She Lies, Philipp Roller, Sugartin and A Youth. Across more than two decades, REWORK’s tracks have also been handed to Andrew Weatherall, Roman Flügel, Trentemøller, Magda, Paranoid London, Cinthie and Seth Troxler for reinterpretation. They have little need to prove their underground credentials. “Disco Love” sounds more interested in what can still be done with them. Listen to Disco Love Remixes below and order the EP here. items.body: Summer songs traditionally have an unfair advantage. They get cars with the windows down, imprudent decisions, swimming pools, romances improved by temporary geography. Soft Vein’s new single Another Summer seems suspicious of all that. Justin Chamberlain approaches the season as someone might regard an old photograph found in a drawer: with affection, perhaps, but also with the knowledge that whatever happened there has already escaped its participants. The title suggests recurrence, but Chamberlain sounds interested in what recurrence fails to restore. Another season comes around. The people inhabiting it have changed. The song, the final single from Soft Vein’s forthcoming All We’ve Known of Heaven, has some of the suave composure of Robert Palmer and the eccentric pop intelligence of John Foxx and Peter Gabriel. A rounded bass line moves beneath clipped vocal phrases and lush synthesizers, which periodically rise around Chamberlain without swallowing him. The staccato chant and hook are especially good, giving an otherwise sumptuous ballad a curious nervousness, as though somebody has prepared the perfect sentence and then discovered that speaking it aloud changes its meaning. This year, Soft Vein has moved further toward synthpop, although Chamberlain retains a detached, cerebral chill. Another Summer may be the most persuasive argument yet for that development: a beautiful arrangement can make emotional confusion more acute. The bass has an almost tactile roundness; the keyboards occasionally widen into luminous sheets; his voice stays exposed in the middle, stylish without becoming mannered. Every element appears to know exactly how much room it should occupy. Chamberlain sings softly, often close enough to conversational volume that his restraint becomes part of the song’s psychology. Soft Vein has always been interested in the humiliations of wanting something from another person: reassurance, sex, permanence, an explanation. Another Summer finds him contemplating communication; his delivery has the attractive uncertainty of a person willing to disclose something before deciding whether disclosure was wise. That divided temperament has followed Soft Vein from 2023’s Pressed in Glass through Through Blinds, the 2024 record that brought Chamberlain’s songwriting into sharper focus. The 2025 EP From Another Room, featuring remixes by Twin Tribes and Qual alongside covers of formative artists, offered a useful bridge. All We’ve Known of Heaven is now available for preorder ahead of its release through Artoffact Records. Soft Vein will mark the album with a September 11 Los Angeles release show at Zebulon, presented by Minty Boi, with Catherine Moan as direct support and Secret Attraction opening. Buy tickets here. items.body: Horror Vacui Shadows Sanctuary Artoffact Records The layoff taken by Italian goth rock vets Horror Vacui since their last record has resulted in a new label and some line-up shuffling, but if you’ve tracked the path they’ve walked since their 2012 debut it won’t surprise you to learn that those aren’t the only things new to Shadows Sanctuary. A good ways removed from the crust influenced deathrock of In Darkness You Will Feel Alright, their fifth LP is a more integrated yet less showy affair than anything they’ve yet attempted. They might not be immediately apparent, but subtler moves like the harmonic colour on the chorus of opener “Dispossed” playing off the tight but sparse post-punk rhythm of the verse are more reflective of Shadows‘ priorities, and indeed, the slow winnowing away of the band’s punk roots and the uptick in more spidery and moody pure goth rock feels like it’s finally reached its apotheosis with this record. Oddly, that shift doesn’t yield more of the ascendant anthems (a la “Consolation Prize”) or compositional experiments (“Unreachable”) that the preceding LP Living For Nothing hinted at as their future. Instead, it’s more measured and reflective fare, like the lilting roll of “Eventide”, which is representative of Shadows Sanctuary. Even in the LP’s most raucous moments, like the scaling leads of “A Sunny Day” which slide overtop a dead simple thumping beat, the band sounds more akin to the theatrical excess of 90s acts like Corpus Delicti than any deathrock forbearer you’d care to name. Similarly, the instrumentation and arrangement of “Midnight” are simple enough, but it ends up having a plaintive if not downright romantic cast. “Skyless Eyes” is plenty propulsive, but the focus stays on atmosphere rather than aggression. It’s tempting to speculate as to the reasons behind this shift in Horror Vacui’s sound during their break – previous guitarist Marzia shifting to the drumkit, the arrival of new guitarist Vasu, the pandemic, the irresistible drift towards “mature” records – but again, a general sense of drift between dark rock subgenres has been part and parcel of the band for a while. They’ve long used the motto “punker than dark, darker than punk” to express this ambiguity, and while it still holds in theory on Shadows Sanctuary, the record does find one half of that dichotomy eclipsing the other. Buy it. Shadows Sanctuary by Horror Vacui The post Horror Vacui, “Shadows Sanctuary” appeared first on I Die: You Die.

items.body: Crucifera, the solo industrial project of New Jersey-based musician Danielle Astraea, released the single “Paint” on July 24, 2026. The track is self-released independently and available digitally on Bandcamp and other streaming platforms. It follows the debut album, “Exostential,” released April 3, 2026. “Paint” mixes industrial, trip-hop, gothic trap and witch-house elements. Astraea wrote, produced, recorded and mixed the track herself in her home studio, and Sebastian Komor (Icon of Coil, Xenomorph Productions) handled mastering, the same role he held on “Exostential.” The song is a dark, abrasive exploration of cognitive dissonance, attribution error and tribalistic projection, built around how people reduce other people to fixed caricatures – either idealized or demonized – rather than responding to who they actually are. Astraea describes her overall sound as “crunchy ethereal industrial music for spiders.” She works without a traditional drum kit, building the rhythm tracks from processed field and sound-design textures rather than sampled or programmed drum sounds, and composes each song first on acoustic piano and guitar before building out the electronic production in her home studio. Paint by crucifera About Crucifera Crucifera is the solo project of Danielle Astraea, a self-taught multi-instrumentalist, producer and visual artist based in New Jersey, United States. Astraea began her professional career in the arts and creative direction in 2000, but kept her original music private for years before releasing it under the Crucifera name. She writes, records, mixes and produces every Crucifera track herself, starting each composition on acoustic piano or nylon guitar before building the finished arrangement digitally in her home studio. Crucifera’s debut full-length album, “Exostential,” was released on April 3, 2026, preceded by the singles “saVior” and “Martyr Box.” The album was mastered by Sebastian Komor of Icon of Coil and Xenomorph Productions; “Martyr Box” was mixed by Steven Seibold of Hate Dept. Astraea has also contributed composition and remix work to other industrial acts outside her solo output. “Paint,” Crucifera’s first single since “Exostential,” continues the project’s fusion of acoustic songwriting roots and industrial electronic production, with Komor again handling mastering. A new Crucifera EP is planned for later in 2026, followed by a second full-length album in 2027.
items._cn_summary: Crucifera是新泽西音乐人Danielle Astraea的个人工业计划，2026年7月发布单曲《Paint》，延续首张专辑《Exostential》的风格路径。歌曲融合工业、trip-hop、哥特陷阱与巫术浩室元素，主题围绕认知失调、基本归因谬误与部落式投射——人们如何将他人简化为固定的漫画式形象。创作上，Astraea独立完成词曲、编曲、录音与混音，摒弃传统鼓组，以处理过的田野录音与声音设计素材构建节奏层，每首歌先以原声钢琴或尼龙弦吉他起稿，再在家庭工作室中拓展为电子编制。母带由Icon of Coil成员Sebastian Komor操刀。艺术家自述其音乐为"脆响空灵工业，供蜘蛛聆听"。后续计划于年内推出EP，2027年发行第二张全长专辑。

items.body: Korean vocalist Hye-gang and Polish producer DustCats have released “Tired with all these, for restful death I cry”, a single continuous drone and ambient piece running just over 35 minutes, on the Wrocław netlabel Ubocze Rec. (catalog Ubocze Rec. 089). The digital release went up on Bandcamp on August 7, 2026, as a name-your-price download with a suggested price of 27 and a minimum of 10. The track’s title is drawn from the opening line of Shakespeare’s Sonnet 66. It builds from field recordings DustCats made in Bangkok, Thailand, layered with a generative drone assembled from six Thai-sourced samples controlled through sliders and macros in Ableton. Over that bed, Hye-gang reads a William Wordsworth poem and Sonnet 66 in a spoken-word style DustCats describes as “very ASMR.” The music was recorded in Wrocław, Poland, while the cover artwork and an accompanying video were shot in Jelenia Góra, Poland, using a microscope attachment on a phone camera. DustCats describes the piece’s assembly: “While in Thailand a while ago, I made a lot of field recordings, but after returning, I had no idea how to put them together. Meanwhile, Hye-gang, a friend from Korea with whom I’d already collaborated on Ashes and Kalpa, sent me her recordings, where she reads a Wordsworth poem and Shakespeare’s Sonnet 66. […] I also experimented with a generating drone that combined six different samples, which could be controlled using sliders and macros in Ableton. All the samples were Thai ones. All this, combined, resulted in a 35-minute suite recorded at once.” Tired with all these, for restful death I cry by Hye-gang \ DustCats About Hye-gang and DustCats DustCats is a Poland-based producer who builds drone and ambient pieces from field recordings, active on Ubocze Rec., the Wrocław netlabel run by Łukasz Bejnar and Kuba Knoll since 2019. Hye-gang is a South Korea-based vocalist and collaborator who contributes spoken-word readings to DustCats’ productions; by DustCats’ own account, the pair had previously worked together on releases titled “Ashes” and “Kalpa” before “Tired with all these, for restful death I cry.” Ubocze Rec. operates as a non-commercial netlabel associating solo acts and projects from across electronic and experimental music, with releases spanning industrial, field recordings, lo-fi, ambient, techno, electro and IDM. The label’s catalog is anchored by Łukasz Bejnar’s own recording alias Uchylak, whose 2025 album “Zimna Gmina” received prior Side-Line coverage; label artist Dariusz Jackowski’s EP “Bezimienny” was also covered by Side-Line following its August 2026 release. “Tired with all these, for restful death I cry,” released alongside two other Ubocze Rec. titles on August 7, 2026, extends that catalog into a two-person, cross-continental field-recording piece built from source material gathered in Thailand, Poland and South Korea.
items._genre: drone / ambient / field recording / spoken word
items._cn_summary: 这是一则来自Side-Line的专辑发行介绍，乐评性质较弱。韩国声乐家Hye-gang与波兰制作人DustCats合作，发行了35分钟单曲《Tired with all these, for restful death I cry》，标题取自莎士比亚第66号十四行诗。作品以DustCats在曼谷采集的田野录音为底，叠加六个泰国采样的生成式drone，Hye-gang以类似ASMR的语态朗读华兹华斯诗作与莎翁十四行诗。整首曲子一次录制完成于波兰弗罗茨瓦夫。封面与配套视频在波兰Jelenia Góra用手机显微镜附件拍摄。发行厂牌为波兰netlabel Ubocze Rec.，实行自定价格数字下载。该作品结合了实验电子、田野录音、文本朗读等元素，具有跨文化合作的小规模制作特点，但文本本身以资讯陈述为主，缺乏深度评论分析。

items.body: Project Pitchfork, the Hamburg group that mixes dark wave, electro-industrial and dark electro elements, released “Quantum Mechanics” on 12 August 2011 through Trisol. The album turns 15 this year. It arrived one year after “Continuum Ride” (2010) and appeared on CD, as a strictly limited double-CD book edition of 2,000 copies, and digitally. Peter Spilles wrote and produced the album, Chris von Rautenkranz mastered it at Soundgarden Tonstudio, Ingo Römling created the artwork and Jens Howorka took the band photography. The ten-track album runs “Freeze in Silence,” “Lament,” “Run for Cover,” “Radical Business,” “Mute Spectators,” “Quantum Mechanics,” “The Queen of Time and Space,” “Splice,” “We Will Descend” and “You Rest in My Heart.” The book edition, bound with thread stitching and packed with a 40-page booklet of lyrics and additional artwork, adds a bonus disc holding the exclusive tracks “Tempest” and “Insomnia,” remixes of “Freeze in Silence,” “Run for Cover” and “Lament,” and an instrumental version of the title track. In December 2019, Trisol reissued “Quantum Mechanics” as a limited 2LP and 2CD set. The album streams on Spotify. About Project Pitchfork Project Pitchfork started in Hamburg, Germany, where vocalist and composer Peter Spilles and keyboardist Dirk Scheuber began collaborating in 1989. The pair played their first concert in Hamburg in February 1990 and recorded the demo “K.N.K.A.” that same year. Their debut album “Dhyani” followed in May 1991 on Hypnobeat, and 1992 brought both “Lam-‘Bras,” which introduced vocalist Patricia Nigiani, and “Entities.” In 1994 the band moved to Off Beat for “IO,” whose singles “Renascence” and “Carrion” brought them into the German charts. A year later they founded their own imprint Candyland Entertainment, issued “Alpha Omega” and supported Rammstein on selected tour dates. The late 1990s produced “¡Chakra:Red!” and the concept album “Eon:Eon,” while the 2000s added “Daimonion,” the “NUN” trilogy built around “Inferno,” and “Kaskade” (2005). On Trisol, the group released “Dream, Tiresias!” and “Continuum Ride” before “Quantum Mechanics” arrived in August 2011. “Black” (2013), “Blood” (2014) and “Look Up, I’m Down There” (2016) followed, and the space-oriented trilogy of “Akkretion,” “Fragment” and “Elysium” was completed in 2024. The current line-up centres on Peter Spilles with keyboardist Jürgen Jansen and drummers Achim Färber and Christian “Leo” Leonhardt; co-founder Dirk Scheuber left the group in 2021. The 15th anniversary of “Quantum Mechanics” places the album back in that timeline, early in the band’s 2010s run on Trisol.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章并非传统意义上的乐评，而是Project Pitchfork专辑《Quantum Mechanics》发行15周年的纪念性新闻稿。文章主要罗列了专辑的基本信息：十首曲目列表、幕后制作人员（Peter Spilles创作、Chris von Rautenkranz母带处理）、限量版双CD书装的收藏细节（2000册、40页歌词册）、以及2019年的黑胶再版信息。乐队历史部分简要追溯了从1990年首演到2024年完成太空三部曲的演变轨迹。全文缺乏对音乐本身的听觉分析、审美评价或创作背景的深入探讨，更像是唱片档案的资料性整理。对于关心暗潮与工业电子流派的听众来说，文章提供了完整的发行脉络与曲目索引，但未能触及声音设计的具体细节或作品的艺术价值。

I want to personally direct you to a remarkable piece of music titled "Two Views of a Prayer," composed and written by
David Dzubinski
as part of the
Prism Quartet
's new series of collaborations called
Unlocking Your Inner Composer
. If you have listened to my radio programs, you are probably familiar with the quartet's ground-breaking, genre-blurring music. If not, there's no better introduction than this.
Performed in November of 2025 at the Free Library of Philadelphia, they invited vocalist
Ursula Rucker
, percussionist
Tyshawn Sorey
, and violinist
Carlos Santiago
to collaborate on the arrangement and performance of Dzubinski's composition. It travels from raw to lyrical and back in the course of just under 4 minutes, with both finesse and energy. - Cliff Furnald, editor

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣圈资深歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔，收录五首曲目。乐队成员各自带来不同的音乐视角，作品以传统民谣为主，辅以一件乐队成员Morten Musicus创作的原创新作。开篇曲《Svennedal》以粗犷的小跑节奏展现了主唱极具说服力的嗓音；口簧与风笛为唯一原创曲《Nordgård》注入了持续推进的动力；扬琴为传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》铺垫了细腻的背景层次；终曲《Orms》作为纯器乐曲，以口簧、长笛与弦乐的交织营造出既灵动又略带失衡的张力。整体氛围古老而略带粗粝感，展现出远超新人水准的成熟度。作品融合了北欧传统民谣元素与实验性的器乐编排，但创新维度较为有限。

items.body: Review by XixoTheRock — Rodrigo San Mart�n is mostly known as an argentinian niche, musician oriented content creator, hehas a decent presence on the community and has, alongside bands like Qu�sar (which I've reviewedpreviously) organized progressive rock festivals in the recent years, he's a relevant figure in theargentinian underground scene although his music remains relatively obscure, he currently works as amusic teacher.He's had a LOT of projects both solo and band oriented, and as he himself has stated, for a while heleft music and composed only to himself, due to the lack of commercial success and recognition,which is a sad assessment of the reach and interest of the general public on prog rock. Still hiswork remains high quality and interesting, this, "Otro d�a en la distop�a" is his latest LP release,it dwells on relevant topics ranging from surveillance states, algorithmic numbness, the destructionof communities and life after the pandemic...therefore, it *will be a strongly emotional album*.As it is my tradition, I would like to start off by dissecting the quality of the compositionsthemselves, which, is quite consistent throughout the entirety of the album's run-time. The range ofthe compositions oscillates between two (theoretically as in practice it *works*) opposing forces :Heavy, energetic and aggressive vs emotional, quiet and intimate music. These 2 blocks are bestrepresented by the 2 opening tracks, "Las palabras que negu�" (a track that opens and closes thealbum as it's split in two parts, just as "Shine on you crazy diamond" and "The sky moves sideways"were) is by far the album's emotional core, intimate, slow and deliberately tension-building, thetrack relies on a piano and guitar leitmotifs alongside sensitive, jazz, tango and ballad likerhythms overlaped with ambient textures, the track builds tension that is released with a swirlingand bluesy guitar solo, a feeling which inspires images of cozy blankets on an otherwise bad day, itresembles Pink Floyd and Porcupine tree's early works (I didn't mention them just as a fun fact!)and the small acoustic moments are like the golden hour, this bloc of (mellow) songs can beinterpreted as representations of a decaying humanity and the mental health crisis we are currentlyexperiencing as a society. On the other bloc, the title track "Otro d�a en la distop�a" is heavy,flute leaning (very akin to bands like Jethro Tull and Spanish band M�go de �z) and has a hightempo, aggressive playing and lots of distortion, with a slower paced yet still as energetic chorusthat has a mellotron in it, it represents the aggressive most machine like side of modern society...despite that, I consider the actual heavy song of the album is "La mirada que devuelve el reflejo"which has an absolute killer riff. Overall, the compositions are all very interesting and consistentin quality, each one is creative and takes a spin on already established music tendencies,therefore, despite being progressive, they are actually quite easy to digest, this recalls an auraof bands like argentinian group "Sui generis", and Spanish bands "Extremoduro" and "Asfalto", everysingle track is quite enjoyable and they all keep the same emotional core which is an aura ofnumbness, loss, confusion, fear and paranoia, I could definitely picture myself reading HoracioQuiroga's works (yes I know he's Uruguayan but still) to the instrumental sections of the record.Without getting too much into the production, I can say it's crystal clear, this is incredibleconsidering the fact that, after all, this is a record that was recorded, mixed and mastered on ahome studio, settings like that don't usually end up making gourmet production but this isn't thecase, granted San Mart�n is both as technically formed an engineer and a musician. You can feel theweight and dread of every instrument and the pitches hit precisely in tune, the way the layers arearranged and programmed on the Bandcamp software is milimetrically precise, nothing is ever off abeat, the mixing is great although I could actually enjoy the album a little more if the bass wasmore audible and there's no problems like reverberation, feedback, bloated audio etc. For being aone man project, the production is as precise as if it were done by a team of professionals on agreat studio.Now...not everything is sunshine, lollipops and rainbows, this album has two fatal flaws thatseverely hurt the experience and lower the quality of the record overall, these two flaws being thelyrics and the vocals.I'll start with the vocals...and I'd like to compare it to the situation of Rush's early records,remember how Geddy Lee used to sign obnoxiously high pitched, like he wasn't breathing and superrough? Yeah that also sums up the situation of the vocals here perfectly. San Mart�n attempts tosing WAY higher than his actual vocal range and tries to keep his voice soft and heartfelt, thesetwo end up turning into a negative feedback and they both end up harming the record. His voice isdifficult to listen through most of the records, specially in those moments where he adds littlechoruses and secondary vocal lines, eclipsing the wonderful instrumentals with rough vocals. Attimes this can make you even want to stop listening to the record all together since it is so onyour face and difficult to dismiss, taking into account that San Mart�n is a professional, skilledmusician, this is also contradictory to his training, and is something he could actually improve. (As a side note, his new band "Auguria" released a single around 2 months ago, where anothervocalist is doing the singing and that only shows how prominent this problem is on his own soloworks [despite the single not being great either])The lyrics are also quite poor, despite dealing with visceral, relevant and deeply polemic topicsrelated to our new status quo, something which should result in string lyrics, they are very cliche,hollow and amateurish, not nearly as polished compared to other contemporary Hispanic bands of thisday and era like Chilean band Hesse Kassel, nor do they live up to San Mart�n's inspirations such asRoger Waters. They don't really do justice to the topics, and explore them so dimly and on such asurface level, non metaphoric ("I don't want to be one's and zero's, really? We're talking about a compatriot of Benedetti, Cort�zar and Borges...come on) way that they are not a good piece of poetry by any means. Add this tomy previous critique to the records vocals and you'll understand why I say this significantlyhinders the experience you can get out of this album.Overall, it's an album of mixed quality, technically and musically impressive but weak lyrically andthus, emotionally (as lyrics are what's most important to emotions in concept albums, with theexception of adaptations to literary works such as camel's "The snow goose"), it's something I'drecommend to symphonic rock fans but adding the nuance of it's strong downsides, it's an enjoyable record despite it's flaws, instrumentally wonderful, weak on concept execution and lyrics...it's a piece of art that will resonate more with those who value instrumentation over lyrics.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张阿根廷地下前卫摇滚专辑，评论者详细剖析了作品的两种对立美学：内省、亲密的情感段落与重拍、激进的器乐爆发。开篇作品横跨专辑首尾，借鉴了Pink Floyd式结构铺陈，以钢琴与吉他动机配合爵士、探戈与抒情节奏律动，营造出缓慢积蓄的张力，最终在布鲁斯吉他独奏中释放。标题曲则走向另一极端，长笛主导、密集失真与mellotron交织，呈现机械式的社会批判意象。整张专辑围绕监控国家、算法麻木、社群瓦解等主题展开，情感浓度较高，作曲质量在全场曲目中保持一致的水准。作为来自非主流音乐地区的独立创作，作品在传统前卫摇滚框架内融入了南美节奏元素与地下场景的文化语境，但整体仍属于类型内的扎实创作，未明显突破既有范式。

items.body: German post-punk and darkwave act Escape With Romeo released their 13th studio album, “Night After Night”, on August 7, 2026 through Zeitklang. The Cologne band’s new release arrives on CD digipak and digital, and follows the group’s 2024 comeback album “Suspicious Bliss”. Night After Night by Escape With Romeo ‘Night After Night’ tracklist and credits “Night After Night” runs 14 tracks: “Edit Me Out”, “No Turning Back”, “Sound and the Fury”, “Something That Lasts”, “New World Order”, “Cancel Anytime”, “I Need Something Stronger”, “Fear’s a Ghost”, “Little Did I Know”, “Night After Night”, “Skyscraper Spiders”, “I’m My Own Worst Enemy”, “You Need the Drugs” and “Wrong Side of Town Pt. 2”. All songs are written by singer, guitarist and songwriter Thomas Elbern, except “You Need the Drugs”, a cover of the 2013 WestBam track featuring Richard Butler of the Psychedelic Furs, credited here to its writers Klaus Jankuhn, Maximilian Lenz and Butler. The album was recorded, mixed and produced by Elbern and drummer Frenzy Erl at Zeitklang in Brühl and Highline in Munich between January 2025 and June 2026, and mastered by Erl. Elbern handles vocals, guitars, synths, vocoder and samples, with Frenzy Erl on drums, Tobias Schwartz on bass and Stella Tonon on vocals. Artwork and graphic design are by schmalfett.com. Themes and rollout The band describes “Night After Night” as harder, more emotional and more direct than “Suspicious Bliss”, the direction Elbern set out to push further at the start of 2025. Songs including “No Turning Back” and “New World Order” address what the band calls a dystopian zeitgeist shaped by AI, while “Skyscraper Spiders” and “Wrong Side of Town Pt. 2” extend the mood signalled by the single “Fear’s a Ghost”. Press materials for the release describe it as “somewhere between post-rock, trip-hop, and the much overused term post-punk.” “Night After Night” was preceded by the singles “Fear’s a Ghost”, released on February 6, 2026, and “Sound and the Fury”, which Side-Line covered as the third single from the album in March 2026. The band will support the album with a Germany tour in autumn 2026, performing as a trio and mixing songs from “Night After Night” with material from across its history. About Escape With Romeo Escape With Romeo was founded in Cologne in 1989 by singer and guitarist Thomas Elbern, who had previously fronted the new wave band Seltsame Zustände and played guitar and wrote songs for Pink Turns Blue. The band’s early catalog appeared through Sound Factory, starting with the self-titled “Escape With Romeo” in 1990 and continuing with “Autumn on Venus” (1991), “Next Stop Eternally” (1993), “Blast of Silence” (1996) and “How Far Can You Go” (1998), a run that included the early single “Somebody”, the band’s best-known track from that period. Keyboardist Martin Pott joined from the second album onward. From 2001 the band’s releases moved to Zeitklang, the label Elbern runs himself, starting with “Come Here White Light” (2001) and continuing through “Love Alchemy” (2002), “Psalms of Survival” (2004), “Emotional Iceage” (2007), “Samsara” (2012) and “After the Future” (2015). Escape With Romeo announced its farewell in 2017, played a final tour in 2018 and had dissolved following festival appearances in 2019. The band returned in 2022 with the double compilation “Based on a True Story – Best of Escape With Romeo”, which led into “Suspicious Bliss”, released on November 1, 2024 as the first new studio album since “After the Future”. The 2026 rollout for “Night After Night” opened with “Fear’s a Ghost” in February, followed by “Sound and the Fury” in March, and now arrives with the album itself on August 7, 2026 via Zeitklang.
items._cn_summary: 德国科隆老牌后朋克与暗潮乐队Escape With Romeo推出第十三张录音室专辑《Night After Night》，延续了乐队自1989年以来的稳定创作路线。专辑共收录14首曲目，全部由主创Thomas Elbern创作，涵盖硬朗吉他riff、合成器音色与人声取样，主题上触及人工智能时代、技术垄断与社会焦虑等议题。制作层面强调情感张力与直接性，较前作更具重量感，风格定位介于后摇滚、trip-hop与后朋克之间。作品在编排上保持类型化框架，融合暗潮的冷峻氛围与电子化的声响处理，但整体走向仍属该流派常规范畴，未展现突出的实验性突破。

items.body: The continuing solo adventures of Elkhorn’s Drew Gardner find the NY-based artist following the groove and exploring within it thoroughly with an expert crew of free improv players skilled in the ways of aural psychedelics. Freshly unleashed by Eiderdown Records, Rabbit Ears rips through juggernaut acid rockers (such as the thunderous title cut that opens the record with a major BANG), slithering dual guitar chases (“Holmdel Horn Antenna” and “Garden Eels”) and drifting meditative soundscapes (“Conch Shell”). With Tom Malach on second guitar and Andy Cush on bass (both from Garcia Peoples) and Ryan Jewell on drums (from…well, nearly everything we cover here on RCU), Gardner plays with a patient looseness born of utter trust in his collaborators while navigating the cosmic waves of prismatic sounds that surge throughout each track. This familiarity and freedom allows for the band’s synergy to bloom into confident, fully kaleidoscopic jams. Each piece glows with a palpable excitement with each musician bringing their absolute best to the table, creating a tight and cohesive supergroup sound (minus the ego!) that would be more fitting for a band ten times their age. With red-hot wah-wah fuzz, bombastic rhythms and an overall mellow yet doomy atmosphere, this is an instant psych-rock classic that even Hendrix himself would have dug. Be sure to grab your copy from Eiderdown on vinyl or digital today. -KH

items._cn_summary: Drew Gardner 作为 Elkhorn 成员的个人项目，与多位自由即兴乐手合作，在迷幻摇滚的框架内进行即兴探索。专辑收录重型的酸性摇滚曲目、双吉他追逐段落以及冥想式的漂浮音景，Tom Malach 担任第二把吉他，Andy Cush 负责贝斯，Ryan Jewell 操鼓。四位乐手之间的高度默契使得整体呈现出松弛而自信的协作质感，吉他音色覆盖哇音与模糊效果，节奏强劲有力，整体氛围兼具迷幻的舒缓与沉重感。作为独立厂牌 Eiderdown Records 的发行，制作保持了地下场景的纯粹性。乐评文字指出这些乐手熟悉彼此的演奏方式，使即兴段落能够自然展开为完整的作品结构。

items.body:
Moving sideways from Warp to Domino, Simian Mobile Disco's James Ellis Ford challenges himself on his second solo full-length, crafting a set of Sakamoto-inspired synth pop from his hospital bed.

Ford's always been capable of producing pitch-perfect pop - his appearance on records from everyone from the Pet Shop Boys to Depeche Mode is a testament to that - but 'Lost in Another World' is a more personal affair. It was written and produced in hospital after he'd been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia last year, "on the ward between rounds of chemo." Thankfully his condition has improved - he posted earlier this month that he's got no more treatment in store - but the album stands as a vulnerable reflection of a difficult time. Ford describes it as a "pep talk", and it draws on some of his most enduring influences, Yellow Magic Orchestra and Japan, to channel its complicated tangle of emotions. 

On the opening track (and lead single) 'Overtones', Ford's voice hovers over plasticky rhythmelodic sequences and rubbery '80s drums and you'd be forgiven for assuming it's a lost city pop demo. Ford doesn't let the energy fall off, either, waltzing through slow-motion melancholia on the tentatively beautiful 'Here Today' and John Foxx-style synth pop on 'This Too Shall Pass'. Ultimately, it's surprisingly hopeful material, infused with genuine feeling.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Simian Mobile Disco成员James Ellis Ford的第二张个人全长作品，从Warp转投Domino厂牌发行。他在确诊急性髓系白血病后，于化疗间隙的病床上完成了整张专辑的创作与制作，因此唱片带有强烈的个人色彩，被作者形容为一次'自我鼓励'。音乐上受Yellow Magic Orchestra和Japan影响，以坂本龙一式的合成器流行为主轴，融入八十年代复古节拍与塑料感的音序器音色。开场曲带有city pop气息，后续曲目在慢速忧郁与John Foxx式的冷调合成器流行之间交替展开。整张专辑在情绪层面出人意料地充满希望，尽管诞生于艰难的处境，仍传递出真实可感的温度，是一张情感真挚、制作精良的私人化合成器流行作品。

items.body: Review by yarstruly — This review is simultaneously published on my blog (Scott's Song by Song Spotlights with links and additional information).Enigmatic Sound Machines (ESM) are a collaboration between Jeremie Arrobas (a founding member of Men Without Hats) and Thomas Szirmay (a prog musicologist, researcher, producer, arranger, actor, vocalist and writer). They are based in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. This is their fourth album since their 2023 debut. According to the information I have received, ESM: "is a retro-futuristic project, the brainchild of two childhood friends with a common love for music, philosophy, and the arts." Today I'll be reviewing their 4th album "Divided by One".Over the years, they have expanded to become a 4-piece band. The line-up for this album is as follows.- Jeremie Arrobas/ lead vocals, synth guitars, keyboards, sound machines- Thomas Szirmay /enigmatic voice and sound machines- Alain Bellaiche/ guitars . backing vocals- Hansford Rowe / bass and backing vocalsGuest artists :- Steve Bonino/guitars (1,6)- Roland Buhlmann/ guitars (7)- Anna Arrobas / backing vocals (1,3,4,7)- Laura Piazzai/ lead vocals (8)- Quinn Bachand / violin (8) This album was provided by Anne-Claire Rallo of Bad Dog Promotions. As always, I receive no further compensation, and I call it like I hear it. As per my usual method, this is a cold listen.Let's listen and find out what all of that means!!Track 1 - Divided by One (6:16)After a few sound effects, a steady drumbeat begins, soon joined by some cool fretless bass work. They lock into a groove, and the guitar plays power chords (Steve Bonino?). Jeramie joins with lead vocals soon after. There is a slight Pink Floyd feel in some ways. The tempo is moderate and the bass part gives it a slightly funky feel. I believe Thomas' "Enigmatic Voice" is in the choruses. I love the overall soundscape. The production is clean and clear. At around 4:30, there are words spoken in what I believe is French. There are some really unique and cool sounds as they begin to bring the song to a close. I really liked that! There are some really different, unique tones, yet it is still accessible to most listeners. And if offering the listener something unique and different isn't progressive, I don't know what is!Track 2 - Chaos Dreaming (9:33)A spooky keyboard sound opens this one. At around 1:20, the rhythm section enters and creates a simple groove. The keyboards and guitar are now playing a melodic motif. About a minute later, the rhythm section temporarily drops out, and they begin a new theme. The vocals come in with the "enigmatic voice". After the 5-minute mark, we get an instrumental break. A reggae groove eventually emerges; I like it. Hansford Rowe has a nice bass tone on this. The vocals return afterwards. The chorus has a catchy hook on the title phrase. The effects that they use are captivating. Cool track, with a potentially ear-worm chorus.Track 3 - Siren Song (5:07)The opening sound effects do indeed invoke the siren's song. The vocals enter and lead the instruments in with a slow groove. This one is a little bit "doom-y". I like the vocal sound with lots of reverb and echoes. The contrast between the heavy doom-laden verses and the somewhat lighter choruses is nice. Good track, very engaging.Track 4 - Pool of Mirrors (5:54)Electric piano with a vibrating tone starts this one out. This one is a little bit lighter at a moderate tempo. The music sort of floats. This is not too far removed from something that 21 Pilots might do (and I am very much on the record that I believe that 21 Pilots are a modern art-rock band). There is even something of a rap at around 3:30. The rhythm section drops out around 4:30 and there is a quieter section. Eventually, the instruments drop off one by one, leaving the main keyboard riff and an acoustic guitar lead. The bass takes over from the guitar, then some wordless vocals bring the song to a close.Track 5 - Heaven's Rain (7:18)This one starts gently with sustained keyboard sounds, electric piano and acoustic guitar. Big tom-tom sounds punctuate the sound before and during the vocals. The "enigmatic voice" is very much in use here. There are some BIG accents just prior to the 2:30 mark. A cool groove keeps the track moving. I like the bass lines on this album. In fact, after 4:30, the bass is featured. I like this instrumental section. It is symphonic much like early King Crimson on "Epitaph". I believe I hear a mellotron. I truly appreciate the fact that even though this is an electronic music project by nature, there are still great dynamic shifts and some real guitars and basses in use. It brings in the human factor. Good track. Track 6 - Screaming Sound Machines (4:57)This begins with an orchestral fade in, then a beat emerges. This has a great groove. The lead vocals are in a low register. I like the feel of this one. At 2:25, there is a bit of a "breakdown" segment with a cool analog synth tone. There is a nice, but brief, guitar solo at around 3:30, presumably from Steve Bonino. This is a pretty cool track. I like the false ending before the final chord.Track 7 - Heavy Water (7:34)A quiet riff over a synth bed starts things off here. Some dissonant piano and sound effects join in. This one is feeling like a slow burn. More sounds enter as we go along. At around the 2-minute mark, the rhythm section makes a beat, and the vocals are downright creepy sounding. I like the refrain of the title with the lead vocals singing other words. Things get quiet for a moment in the middle of the song. The music gets big and powerful at around the 5-minute point. While the drum programming isn't bad, I'd love to hear this with a live drummer, as it's a little stiff sounding sometimes. The rest of the sounds are much more fluid (no pun intended). Track 8 - Inviolate Fields (9:51)The electric piano is the primary sound initially, but the soundscape grows. Guest vocalist Laura Piazzai's voice adds a new dimension to the sound. I already am familiar with her from her work on the Massimo Pieretti album I have reviewed on this blog (see the labels menu); she's wonderful. There is an awesome fretless bass feature at around the 3-minute mark. Quinn Blanchard's violin is kind of spooky in the way that Jimmy Page's bowed guitar is on Led Zeppelin's "In the Evening"; cool! There is a vibraphone tone that is sort of dominating the sound at around 5 minutes, that buries Laura's vocals in the mix, I wish she was brought out more. She comes out more as the song progresses. The overall feel is pretty laid-back on this longest track. I like the triangles or whatever the percussion sounds they are using are at around 8:30. The track just sort of winds down at the end. Piazzai's voice is the stand-out feature of this track. Track 9 - Are Friends Electric? (5:17)This is a cover of a Gary Numan song. A cool bass riff is the motif on this one. This one is moderately fast. The vocal melody is kind of catchy. There is a low-register spoken word section in the middle with a cool rhythmic backdrop. This one has a bit of an 80s new-wave vibe. There is another spoken-word section with about one minute remaining. They ride the riff out to the song's conclusion. OVERALL IMPRESSIONS:Electronic music isn't my biggest area of expertise, but I generally liked this album. The biggest drawback is the drum machine in my opinion. Hansford Rowe's bass playing is so strong and provides a real human element to the sound, but sometimes the drum machine fills were so stiff and mechanical that they didn't quite mesh. I understand that they are coming from a point of view of being "sound machines", so maybe that is what they are going for. From my perspective, however, adding a live drummer would improve their overall sound and be less distracting than the stiff drum machine is to me. There was a lot that I DO like about this album. There are some great riffs and soundscapes and musical concepts here. The vocal sounds, even the processed ones, are very engaging and interesting. Rowe's bass work is a real standout for me. Alain Bellaiche seems to be a good guitarist when he gets the spotlight. This album is really about the electronic sounds that the founding pair of Jeremie Arrobas and Thomas Szirmay bring to the table, however, and in that aspect, they have succeeded. The guest musicians, particularly Steve Bonino, Laura Piazzai, and Quinn Blanchard add a lot to the album. I'll give this an overall score of 4 out of 5 stars (80%), but fans of electronic music stylings will probably like it even more.
items._cn_summary: Enigmatic Sound Machines 是由 Men Without Hats 创始成员 Jeremie Arrobas 与音乐研究者 Thomas Szirmay 合作的四重奏，2026年发行的《Divided by One》是其第四张专辑。乐评以冷听方式逐曲解析：开篇曲以无品贝斯律动和粉红 Floyd 式氛围铺陈，融合法文念白和独特音效；九分半的第二曲以阴森的键盘音色起手，中段插入雷鬼律动和器乐间奏，'enigmatic voice' 人声点缀其间，旋律动机在节奏段落中反复推演；后续曲目因文本截断未能完整描述。整体呈现复古未来主义的折衷主义姿态，融合了前卫摇滚、流行旋律和实验音效，定位为对大多数听众仍具可听性的跨界作品。
